audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Jax Levels 3, 4-5 and first item and gave Gnar Level 6, while the page's own why-strings call those stages "a genuine coinflip", "nets out even", "a wash" and "trade evenly". Difficulty also read TRICKY 7.5/10 on a 51.31% matchup.
audit.why: Packet chart is Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Jax and the mirror flipped to exactly that. The prose was already right; only the side tokens and the difficulty band disagreed.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 through first item flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved, and diff/tone/diffRating/difficulty/final-rating all brought to EVEN 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as your Grandmaster spike and the first-item row as a forced-fight window.
audit.why: GNAR! is Rage-gated, not level-gated — Gnar has it available in Mega form long before 6 and its 90/60/30s cooldown only starts mattering late. Neither champion gains a lane-breaking spell at 6, so the stage swings purely on his transform timer.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and first-item whys rewritten around the Rage bar, with GNAR!'s 90s rank-1 cooldown and Mega Hop's 22s written into the cooldown block.

audit.why: The decisive interaction is already stated correctly and repeatedly: Counter Strike dodges attacks only, so Boomerang Throw's poke, Wallop's stun and the GNAR! wall-slam all pass through it. The kit text agrees — E dodges incoming attacks, and all three of those are abilities. Left alone.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Gnar's GNAR! is down.
edits.after: No Counter Strike until 3, so his boomerang and Hyper autos chip you for free. Farm the level out.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gnar must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike online: eat his walk-up autos, stun, then Q in with W loaded. He can Hop off your head, so it stays even.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around GNAR!'s cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: It lives on his Rage bar: with the transform down you win the trade, with it up Wallop and GNAR! go straight through your dodge.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gnar's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Neither of you gains a lane-breaking spell at 6 — GNAR! is Rage-gated, not level-gated, so the stage swings only on his transform.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity Force lands, but his boomerang poke and transform burst still trade back evenly.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. E or avoid transform. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — 90s at rank 1 and gated on Rage, and the wall-slam stun ignores your dodge. - Mega Hop: 22s at rank 1, his gap-close. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track GNAR! and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you read his Rage bar and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Gnar carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Gnar carry threat 8/10.

notes: The ability work on this page is already at the bar — Counter Strike being attacks-only against Boomerang Throw, Wallop and the GNAR! wall-slam is stated everywhere it should be, so I left the interaction prose alone. Two things for the user: (1) the whole content layer of this matchup is written in FIRST person ("I leap onto his mini body") while every other Jax page is second person — that is a voice inconsistency across the site, not something a per-field length-banded edit can fix, so it needs a deliberate pass; (2) the packet's suspectNames flags on "Counter Strike's", "Hold Counter Strike" and "My Counter Strike" are false positives — the ability name is correct in all three.
